findings.title: Mockery reaches the public prayer summons
findings.claim: The focus warning about making dīn an object of mockery and play becomes, in the immediate context, a warning about converting an audible, community-forming summons to prescribed worship into amusement.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrence of لَعِبًا and هُزُوًا meets the repeated formula in 5:58; نَادَيْتُمْ supplies the raised summons, صَّلَوٰةِ supplies the prescribed worship, and يَعْقِلُونَ supplies the restraint that would preserve the summons' directive force.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see public religious coordination inside the broader phrase about trivializing religion: the issue reaches the handling of a signal that gathers people for ordered worship.
findings.containment: The 5:58 scene gives a concrete local instance of the focus warning. It does not reduce dīn to prayer, make every play-form an audible act, or turn every form of amusement into this ritual case.

epistemic.reason: The channel support is trusted and the exact 5:58 Arabic supplies the local contact; the corroborating HFT record is legacy_unbound, and its unresolved branch roles are therefore retained as attributed evidence.

branch_activations.activation: The focus play term meets its immediate contextual repetition, making the play a recoding of a serious communal act rather than an unqualified description of amusement.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The named trivialization includes turning an ordered religious summons into play.
branch_activations.boundary: This is the local prayer-call instance supplied by 5:58; it does not make every occurrence of play a ritual claim.

branch_activations.boundary: This diagnosis belongs to the prayer-call scene in 5:58; it does not define every form of humor as irrational.

findings.title: Proximity becomes a concealed threshold
findings.claim: The focus's warning about choosing awliyāʾ gains a threshold reading when 5:61 places a professed entry before disbelief carried in and carried out, then names what is concealed: high-trust proximity can carry an unchanged inner stance across the community's boundary.
findings.mechanism: The focus branch of unbroken nearness meets the context sequence of entering, leaving, and concealing. The entry and exit forms give proximity a crossing shape, while concealment explains why an outward profession cannot disclose the durable orientation moving through it.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the relational category matters beyond an overt label: the risk lies in what close access can carry across a threshold while remaining hidden.
findings.containment: The focus still addresses proximity and allegiance among named groups. The context supplies a live concealed-commitment scenario; it does not classify every visitor, every alliance, or every profession of faith as deceptive.

epistemic.reason: The exact Arabic anchors and word coordinates are supplied, but the three contextual branch roles are legacy_unbound and unresolved; they are retained only as attributed roles returning through the focus awliyāʾ occurrence.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Arada ayırıcı unsur olmadan yakın, bitişik veya yanında olma.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus plural أَوْلِيَاءَ carries unbroken nearness or being alongside.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 5:61 places a profession of faith before entry with disbelief, exit with it, and concealed inner content.
branch_activations.activation: The entry-exit sequence gives the focus's proximity a permeable-threshold shape: closeness can carry a concealed stance across the boundary.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The prohibition on taking awliyāʾ includes guarding high-trust proximity against concealed commitments that pass into and out of the community.
branch_activations.boundary: This retains a contextual threshold reading; it does not make every entrant or every close relation a concealed opponent.

branch_activations.carrier: The context form at 5:61 word 6 is attributed as movement into an interior.

branch_activations.activation: The attributed inward crossing turns awliyāʾ proximity into access across a social interior whose contents may remain concealed.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus warning can include scrutiny of what is carried inward through close access.
branch_activations.boundary: No registered branch descriptor is supplied; the reading is limited to the exact attributed inward-crossing role.

branch_activations.activation: The attributed exit completes the threshold movement, showing proximity as a passage that can leave the carried stance unchanged.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The relational warning includes the possibility that a concealed orientation crosses out after having crossed in.
branch_activations.boundary: The exact exit role is retained without a broader unprovided branch meaning or a universal judgment on departures.

branch_activations.carrier: The context form at 5:61 word 16 is attributed as concealment.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The context sets concealment after a verbal profession and the completed entry-exit sequence.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed concealment explains why an outward claim of faith cannot by itself disclose the durable stance carried through awliyāʾ proximity.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's relational boundary becomes sensitive to hidden commitments that surface language leaves undisclosed.
branch_activations.boundary: This is an attributed concealment role from 5:61, not an assertion that the focus names a universal test of inward faith.

findings.title: Protection permits uncompromised witness
findings.claim: The focus's support relation and command of God-directed protection gain a public-witness reading through 5:67: reliance can be relocated from compromising patrons to divine holding so that delivery remains uncompromised.
findings.mechanism: The focus pairs awliyāʾ as a human support relation with ittaqū as protective separation. 5:67 places open delivery beside an assurance of holding from people, making protection the condition that preserves truthful proclamation rather than a reason to purchase safety through hostile patronage.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the positive work of the command: the protective boundary creates room for faithful speech to remain intact under social pressure.
findings.containment: The focus remains a command to believers concerning alliances and God-directed protection. The 5:67 assurance is kept in its messenger context and used for an attributed relational inference, not as a universal guarantee that removes every danger.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches are accepted lexical records and 5:67 is supplied exactly, while the protection-to-reliance application and its unresolved contextual branch are carried from a legacy_unbound HFT record.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Koruma, zarar ile korunacak şey arasına başka bir araç, katman veya engel koyularak gerçekleştirilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus imperative ٱتَّقُوا۟ carries protective separation by placing a barrier against harm.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 5:67 joins open delivery of the message with God's holding the messenger from people.
branch_activations.activation: The focus protection command meets the context's divine holding, so the barrier is read as preserving religious witness from a compromising source of safety.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: God-directed protection can be heard as the condition that keeps public proclamation intact while harmful alliances remain outside the protected boundary.
branch_activations.boundary: The context assurance remains specifically attached to the messenger; the focus command is not converted into a promise of universal worldly safety.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The named human support relation is placed beside a positive relocation of reliance to God for uncompromised witness.
branch_activations.boundary: This adds a reliance relation to the focus; it does not make every human friendship a compromising patronage tie.

branch_activations.activation: The attributed holding supplies the divine protection that can replace reliance on a hostile patron without interrupting public delivery.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's command includes a relocation of protective dependence that permits truthful proclamation to continue.
branch_activations.boundary: No registered branch descriptor is supplied; only the exact holding role and its focus return are retained.

findings.title: Religion appears as entrusted communal custody
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus regulates who may be entrusted with covenant-shaped communal obedience: its double taking around dīn and awliyāʾ can be heard beside 5:70's taking of a confirmed covenant, so trivializers are unsuitable as those charged with mediating and guarding that order.
findings.mechanism: The two focus forms of taking mark deliberate acquisition and taking-for-oneself; dīn supplies an enacted obedience-order and awliyāʾ supplies the role of support or management. 5:70 joins the same taking field to a binding covenant, giving the focus a custody relation rather than a casual-association frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the prohibition as touching formative custody: who is allowed to shape, carry, and manage a community's obedience matters alongside whether they are socially close.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory institutional reading built from the focus's double taking and the exact 5:70 covenant contact. The focus still plainly regulates relations with mockers and disbelievers; it does not explicitly name an office or ban every social relation.

epistemic.reason: The focus lexical branches are accepted and the 5:70 Arabic is exact, but the custody synthesis and unresolved covenant role come from a legacy_unbound HFT outlier and therefore remain explicitly exploratory.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir nesneye erişme, onu ele geçirme ve kendi denetim alanına alma eylemini anlatır.
branch_activations.carrier: The two focus forms of اتَّخَذَ carry deliberate taking into one's own field of control.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 5:70 says that God took a binding covenant, placing the same taking beside a solemn entrusted object.
branch_activations.activation: The doubled taking around dīn and awliyāʾ meets covenant-taking in 5:70, so the focus's act can be seen as a question of what and whom a community deliberately takes into its custody.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus prohibition includes refusal to take trivializers into the custody of the community's religious order.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not explicitly name an office; this is an exploratory custody relation, not a replacement gloss for اتَّخَذُوا۟.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi kendisi için edinip kendine ait hale getirmeyi anlatır.
branch_activations.carrier: The derived focus forms of اتَّخَذَ carry acquiring something for oneself and making it one's own.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The covenant context joins taking to a confirmed binding object and to a history of messengers being rejected when their message is unwelcome.
branch_activations.activation: The for-oneself acquisition facet turns the focus's relational act toward formative ownership: an actor may be installed as part of what the community treats as its own guiding custody.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The warning can be heard as refusing to make mockers into self-appointed owners or handlers of the community's obedience-order.
branch_activations.boundary: This remains an exploratory extension of the derived taking form; it does not claim that the focus explicitly describes institutional appointment.

findings.title: Dīn receives an accountability horizon
findings.claim: The added Fātiḥa phrase مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ gives the focus word دِينَكُمْ an additional judgment-and-requital horizon: trivializing the religious order also treats lightly an order whose meaning reaches answerability.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrence دِينَكُمْ carries the dīn word, while the exact external occurrence in 1:4 pairs the same word with يوم and names the special day of judgment and requital. That direct lexical contact activates the judgment facet without displacing the focus's obedience-order sense.
findings.reader_payoff: The social warning acquires a visible horizon of accountability: the order being mocked is also an order whose claims culminate in judgment and requital.
findings.containment: The overlay adds the judgment facet at this direct contact. دِينَكُمْ remains the addressed religious obedience and way of life; the added Fātiḥa phrase does not turn every occurrence of dīn into a judgment phrase or replace the focus's plain warning.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch is an accepted lexical record and the external Arabic is supplied exactly; the cross-surah changed reading is an author inference from their direct contact, with no separate support record in the packet.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Hüküm, hesap ve karşılığın gerçekleşeceği özel günü adlandırmak.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus occurrence دِينَكُمْ carries the dīn word whose judgment-and-requital facet is available at this contact.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The added 1:4 occurrence مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ explicitly pairs dīn with the day of judgment and requital.
branch_activations.activation: The direct recurrence of dīn beside يوم selects the judgment-and-requital facet for the focus word, allowing the mocked religious order to be heard against its horizon of answerability.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus warning includes treating lightly an order whose meaning reaches judgment and the giving of consequences.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a local external overlay from 1:4; it adds accountability to the focus word without replacing its obedience-based religious-order sense.
